note: One table, two suites. The terminal-distribution Monte Carlo runs in two implementations that cannot call each other — modules/quant_risk/var.py for the gateway and the Telegram companion, web/lib/mc-distribution.ts for the browser — and both now take the same parameters. This pins the parts a reader has to trust: which resampler a run reports having used, the derived block length both default to, the pairs that are a contradiction rather than a choice, and the loss quantile rule a confidence maps onto. tests/test_mc_resampler.py asserts the Python side, tests/mc-distribution.test.ts the TypeScript, and neither may edit this file to make itself pass.

derivedBlockLength.why: clamped up: a block below 5 bars keeps almost no clustering
the mc-parity fixture's own driver length
clamped down: a block that long is barely a resample

contradictions.why: an i.i.d. draw has no blocks to average
a block of one bar is the i.i.d. draw wearing the other name

lossQuantiles.why: Nearest rank on the (100 - C)th percentile of terminal P&L, negated, so a confidence reads as a positive loss. A negative entry means even that quantile ended in profit, which is a fact and not a floor to clip at zero.
